mainTopic: Silence and consent in קידושין (שדיך vs. לא שדיך), and teachings collected from רבי אסי
overview: The גמרא finishes רבא's proof from a ברייתא: once the money is already in her hands, a woman's silence (שתיקה שלאחר מתן מעות) means nothing. Scholars in פום נהרא challenge this proof in the name of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. רב אחאי pushes back, and רבינא rules that only those who received רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's teaching need to worry about a possible קידושין. Next comes the story of a belt-seller who silently took back her snatched belt. רב נחמן rules she is not מקודשת, because she can say 'I took what was mine.' רבא challenges him from a ברייתא about a grabbed סלע, and the גמרא proves רב נחמן's answer: silence counts as agreement only when the man had already arranged the match (שדיך). The amud then turns to teachings the חכמים collected after רבי אסי died. The first is that land, like a woman, cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה, except through חליפין. The second is that people who handle גיטין and קידושין without knowing the laws are worse for the world than דור המבול, which the גמרא proves from פסוקים in הושע. The amud ends with a challenge about whether a single sin is enough for that punishment, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading 'not wanting' as saying 'no' leads to a strange result
steps.stepSummary: Part of רבא's proof. If 'she did not want' in the ברייתא meant she said 'no,' the ברייתא would end up implying that even a clear 'no' could be קידושין, and that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would it really be קידושין even when she said 'No'? Why would it be? She said 'No'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing one possible reading of the ברייתא and showing that it breaks down. This clears the way for the correct reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the words 'she wanted' (רצתה) and 'she did not want' (לא רצתה). If 'did not want' meant an outright 'no,' the ברייתא would be implying that a 'no' still produces קידושין. That is impossible, because a woman who says 'no' is clearly not agreeing.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: When she said 'No,' would it also be a betrothal?
Why? After all, she said 'No'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's analysis of the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'לא רצתה' as an explicit 'no'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would mean a clear 'no' still counts as קידושין, which is absurd.

steps.title: So silence after the money is given means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The correct reading: 'wanted' means she said 'yes,' and 'did not want' means she stayed silent. This proves that silence after the money was given is not agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean: 'she wanted' means she said 'yes,' and 'she did not want' means she stayed silent. Learn from this: silence after the money has been given counts for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reading failed, the גמרא gives the only reading that works. From it, רבא draws his proof that silence after receiving the money is not a 'yes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'did not want' means silence, then the ברייתא rules that a silent woman is not מקודשת. This becomes the rule that silence after the money is given (שתיקה שלאחר מתן מעות) has no legal weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (opens the only workable reading)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: silence after the money is already in her hands is not agreement to קידושין.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section is a debate over whether this proof really holds up.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that 'she wanted' means she said 'Yes,'
and 'she did not want' means she stayed silent.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁתִיקָה דִּלְאַחַר מַתַּן מָעוֹת –
phrases.english: And learn from this that silence after the money is given
is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only reading left after step 1 ruled out the other one.
steps.raayaObject: Silence after the money is given is not consent to קידושין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about money first given as a deposit

steps.title: פום נהרא: the deposit case is different
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, scholars in פום נהרא reject the proof. In the ברייתא she kept quiet because the coins were a deposit and she feared being liable if she threw them. Here the coins were given as קידושין, so if she did not want them she should have thrown them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: In פום נהרא they challenged this in the name of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: Are the cases alike? There, he gave her the coins as a deposit, so she thinks, 'If I throw them and they break, I will have to pay.' Here, he gave them to her as קידושין. If she really did not want it, let her throw them away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's proof by showing that the ברייתא case and our case are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the deposit case, the coins still belong to the man, so her silence can be explained: she is afraid of damaging his property. In the קידושין case, the coins were handed over to become hers. So keeping them quietly looks like agreement, and the ברייתא cannot prove that silence means nothing here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is acceptable to her, she is happy with it

steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject רבא's ברייתא itself. It only says the ברייתא cannot be used as a proof for our different case.

phrases.english: In פום נהרא they raised a difficulty against it
phrases.notes: פום נהרא is a town in בבל. 'It' means רבא's proof.

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: in the name of רב הונא son of רב יהושע:
Is it comparable?
There, he gave them to her as a deposit,

phrases.aramaic: סָבְרָה: אִי שָׁדֵינָא לְהוּ וּמִיתַּבְרִי – מְחַיַּיבְנָא בְּהוּ,
phrases.english: so she thinks: if I throw them and they break, I will be liable for them.
Here, he gave them to her as betrothal money,
and if it is true that she is not happy with it, let her throw them away!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the point is 'she should have thrown them away.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the use of the ברייתא as a proof, not the ברייתא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A deposit stays the man's property, so her silence has another explanation. קידושין money is meant to become hers.

steps.title: רב אחאי: most women do not know the law
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי answers back: not every woman knows the law, so she does not know she would not be responsible for unwanted קידושין coins. She also thinks that if she throws the coins and they break, she will be liable. So the two cases really are alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי objected: Do all women know the law? Here too she thinks, 'If I throw them and they break, I will be responsible for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי pushes back against the פום נהרא challenge and brings back the comparison to the deposit case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פום נהרא argument assumed she knows that unwanted קידושין coins are not her responsibility. רב אחאי says most women do not know that. So her silence is just as easy to explain as in the deposit case, and רבא's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a sharp rhetorical question)
They are learned in the law

phrases.english: רב אחאי objects:
Is that to say all women are learned in the law?
Here too she thinks:
If I throw them and they break,
I will be liable for their loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרֵיךְ רַב אַחַאי: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ נְשֵׁי דִּינָא גְּמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פום נהרא claim that she would have thrown the coins away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That claim assumes she knows the law. Without that knowledge, she has the same fear of liability as in the deposit case.

steps.title: רב אחא בר רב asks רבינא for the practical ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב sends a question to רבינא: in a case like this, where she took the money and stayed silent, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב sent the question to רבינא: In a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth, someone asks for a practical answer. This sets up רבינא's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between פום נהרא and רב אחאי was not clearly settled. So the question is whether in practice we must worry that she is מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent (a question or answer by message)
In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחָה רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא bar רב sent it before רבינא:
In a case like this, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical ruling after the debate in steps 3-4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in practice, silence after receiving קידושין money creates a doubtful קידושין

steps.title: רבינא: only those who heard the view must worry
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that his circle did not receive רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's teaching, so they do not worry. But those who did receive it should be concerned that she might be מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: We did not hear this teaching of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. You, who did hear it, should be concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his practical answer. Whether to be strict depends on whether your tradition includes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא follows רבא's rule that silence means nothing, since he never received the opposing tradition. Still, he respects that רב אחא בר רב's place holds that tradition, so they should be strict and treat it as a possible קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: We heard, it was passed down to us
Be concerned about it (treat it strictly)

steps.whatToRemember: Silence after the money is given: רבינא's circle treats it as meaningless. Those who received רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's teaching must worry about a possible קידושין.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
We did not hear

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: this teaching of רב הונא son of רב יהושע.
You, who heard it, be concerned about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Those who received רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's teaching must be strict. Others need not be.

steps.title: The story of the belt-seller
steps.stepSummary: A man grabbed a belt from a woman selling belts. When she asked for it back, he asked whether she would be מקודשת to him if he gave it. She took the belt and said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman who was selling belts. A man came and grabbed a belt from her. She said to him, 'Give it to me!' He said, 'If I give it to you, will you be מקודשת to me?' She took it and stayed silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about silence and קידושין. This sets up רב נחמן's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'money' was really her own belt, which he had taken. The question is whether taking it back in silence counts as accepting קידושין.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָה קָא מְזַבְּנָה וַורְשְׁכֵי,
phrases.english: There was a certain woman who was selling belts.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא הָהוּא גַּבְרָא חֲטַף וַורְשְׁכָא מִינַּהּ,
phrases.english: A certain man came and snatched a belt from her.
She said to him: Give it to me!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: אִי יָהֵיבְנָא לִיךְ מִיקַּדְּשַׁתְּ לִי?
phrases.english: He said to her: If I give it to you, will you be betrothed to me?
She took it and was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָה קָא מְזַבְּנָה וַורְשְׁכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case on the same theme of silence and קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: she silently took back her own snatched belt after his offer of קידושין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: she was just taking back her own belt
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that she is not מקודשת. She can say, 'Yes, I took it, but I took what was mine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: She can say, 'Yes, I took it, and I took what was mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the ruling on the belt story: her silent taking proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין needs the man to give her something of value that is his. The belt already belonged to her, so taking it back was simply recovering her own property. It is not a sign that she agreed to anything.
steps.whatToRemember: Taking back your own property in silence is not acceptance of קידושין.

phrases.english: And רב נחמן said:
She can say: Yes, I took it,
but what I took was my own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case told in step 7. This ruling becomes the target of רבא's challenge in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She is not מקודשת, because she can claim she was only taking back her own belt.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the case of the grabbed coin
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: if a man grabbed a סלע from a woman's hand and used it for קידושין, she is מקודשת. This seems to contradict רב נחמן's ruling about the belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן: If a man was מקדש a woman with robbed property, with property taken in a forced sale, or with stolen property, or if he grabbed a סלע out of her hand and was מקדש her with it, she is מקודשת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling about the belt by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the man grabs a coin from the woman and uses that same coin for קידושין, and she is מקודשת. That is just like the belt case, where he grabbed her belt and offered it back as קידושין. So why did רב נחמן say she is not מקודשת?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
Property taken by forcing the owner to sell against her will

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
If he betrothed her with robbed property, or with property taken by force, or with stolen property,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁחָטַף סֶלַע מִיָּדָהּ וְקִדְּשָׁהּ – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת!
phrases.english: or if he grabbed a sela from her hand and betrothed her with it, she is betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in Step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the woman who took back her belt in silence is not מקודשת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that a woman is מקודשת when the man grabbed her own coin and used it for קידושין. That is the same as the belt case, so the ruling seems contradicted.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a man who already arranged the match
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the man had already arranged the marriage with her (שדיך).
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where he had already arranged the match.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling by saying the ברייתא is about a different situation, where the couple had already talked about marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had already arranged the match, her silence clearly means she agrees, so she is מקודשת. In the belt case there was no earlier arrangement, so her silence proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He arranged a match, meaning they had already discussed marriage (related to the word שִׁידּוּךְ)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key distinction of the rest of the סוגיא: silence counts as agreement only when there was an earlier marriage arrangement.

phrases.english: There, it is where he had arranged the match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא applies only where the man had already arranged the match.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that silence after a grabbed coin always creates קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Silence creates קידושין only when there was an earlier arrangement. Without one, as in the belt case, she is not מקודשת.

steps.title: Bringing a ברייתא to prove the arranged versus not-arranged distinction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that an earlier arrangement makes a difference, and quotes a ברייתא about a man who repays a debt with a סלע and then says 'be מקודשת to me with it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you say that there is a difference between where he arranged the match and where he did not? As it was taught in a ברייתא: A man said to a woman, 'Take this סלע that I owe you,' and then he said to her, 'Be מקודשת to me with it.' If this was said at the time the money was given: if she wanted, she is מקודשת; if she did not want, she is not מקודשת. If it was said after the money was given, even if she wanted, she is not מקודשת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רב נחמן's distinction by quoting a ברייתא. The proof itself only becomes clear in the next steps, when the גמרא explains the words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא there was no earlier arrangement. The man was just paying back a debt and then suddenly mentioned קידושין. The key question will be what the ברייתא means by 'she wanted' and 'she did not want.'

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you say this? (a request for a source)
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And from where do you say that it makes a difference to us
between where he arranged the match and where he did not arrange it?
As it was taught: He said to her:
'Take this sela that I owe you,'
and then he went back and said to her, 'Be betrothed to me with it.'
If this was at the time the money was given,
if she wanted, she is betrothed;
if she did not want, she is not betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר מַתַּן מָעוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ רָצְתָה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: If it was after the money was given, even if she wanted, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּשָׁנֵי לַן בֵּין שַׁדֵּיךְ וּדְלָא שַׁדֵּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a source to back up the distinction given in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between a man who arranged the match and one who did not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a man who repays a סלע he owes and then says 'be מקודשת to me with it.'

steps.title: What do 'she wanted' and 'she did not want' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the ברייתא means by 'she wanted' and 'she did not want.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she wanted' mean, and what does 'she did not want' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the exact meaning of the ברייתא's words. This is setting up the next move, where two possible readings will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depends on these two words. If 'did not want' means she said no out loud, silence might count as agreement. If it means she stayed silent, then silence does not count.

phrases.english: What is 'she wanted,' and what is 'she did not want'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'she did not want' means an outright 'no' or silence.

steps.title: It cannot mean that 'did not want' is an outright no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries reading 'she wanted' as saying yes and 'she did not want' as saying no, which would make silence count as קידושין. It rejects this, because then the ברייתא should have just said 'מקודשת' plainly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'she wanted' means she said yes, and 'she did not want' means she said no, then if she was silent it would be קידושין. But then let the ברייתא simply teach 'she is מקודשת,' as it does there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible reading of the ברייתא and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silence counted as agreeing, the ברייתא would not need to say 'if she wanted.' It could just say she is מקודשת, the way it does in the other case. Since it bothered to add 'if she wanted,' silence must not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say 'she wanted' means that she said yes,
and 'she did not want' means that she said no,
then if she was silent, it would be a valid betrothal.
But then let it simply teach 'she is betrothed,' as it does there!
phrases.notes: 'There' points to the earlier deposit case, where if he says it while giving the money, she is simply מקודשת, with no 'if she wanted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'she did not want' as an outright 'no.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If silence counted as agreeing, the ברייתא would have written 'מקודשת' plainly, as it does in the other case, and not 'if she wanted.'

steps.title: Silence means she is not betrothed, because she took what was hers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'she did not want' means she stayed silent, and the ברייתא rules she is not מקודשת. The reason is that she can say, 'Yes, I took it, but I took what was mine.' This proves רב נחמן's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'she wanted' means she said yes, and 'she did not want' means she was silent, and the ברייתא teaches that she is not מקודשת. What is the reason? She can say: 'Yes, I took it, but I took what was mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the ברייתא. Only a clear 'yes' makes her מקודשת, while silence does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא the man had not arranged any match. He was just paying a debt, and she stayed silent, and she is not מקודשת. So without an earlier arrangement, silence when taking money that is owed to her means nothing. Steps 15-16 then set this against the grabbed-coin ברייתא to complete the proof of רב נחמן's distinction.
steps.whatToRemember: Silence while taking back money or an object that is hers does not create קידושין, because she can say 'I took what was mine.' Silence counts as agreement only when the man had already arranged the match (שדיך).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think silence never counts. In the grabbed-coin ברייתא she is מקודשת, because there the man had already arranged the match, so her silence shows she agrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the whole סוגיא together. It explains why רב נחמן ruled the woman with the belt is not מקודשת, and it uses the same words, 'I took what was mine,' that he used there.

phrases.english: Rather, 'she wanted' means that she said 'yes,'
and 'she did not want' means that she was silent,
and it teaches that she is not betrothed.
What is the reason? She can say:
'Yes, I took it, but I took what was mine.'
phrases.notes: These are the same words רב נחמן used for the woman with the belt in Step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after Step 13 rejected the first one, and completes the proof started in Step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without an earlier arrangement, a woman who silently takes money or an object that is hers is not מקודשת, because she can say 'I took what was mine.' This supports רב נחמן's answer to רבא.

steps.title: Without the distinction, the robbery ברייתא would be a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that another ברייתא rules a woman IS מקודשת when a man betroths her with something robbed or grabbed from her. Without רב נחמן's distinction, this would clash with the ברייתא just explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: For otherwise, that other ברייתא would be difficult: if he betrothed her with something taken by robbery, by a forced sale, or by theft, or he grabbed a סלע from her hand and betrothed her with it, she is מקודשת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the first one. This sets up the final proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 we learned that a silent woman who received her own money back is not מקודשת, because she can say 'I took what was mine.' But here a man grabs her own סלע, gives it to her for קידושין, and she is מקודשת. Both cases involve her own money and her silence, so something must separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery: taking something openly by force
A forced sale: taking something against the owner's will, even if paying for it

phrases.english: For otherwise, that one would be difficult:
phrases.notes: He means: if you don't accept רב נחמן's distinction, this other ברייתא becomes a problem.

phrases.english: that if he betrothed her with something taken by robbery, by a forced sale, or by theft,
or he grabbed a סלע from her hand and betrothed her with it,
she is מקודשת!
phrases.notes: Here too it's her own money and she stays silent, yet she is מקודשת, the opposite of step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the one just explained, to show that only רב נחמן's distinction resolves the clash.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's distinction between an arranged match and a non-arranged one
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that a woman betrothed with robbed or grabbed property is מקודשת

steps.title: Proof: one case had an arranged match, the other did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the only way to fit the two ברייתות together is רב נחמן's distinction: where the match was arranged she is מקודשת, and where it was not she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: this one is where he had arranged the match, and that one is where he had not arranged it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof and shows that רב נחמן's distinction is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the grabbing case the man had already arranged the match, so her silence shows she agrees. In the debt case nothing was arranged, so her silence can mean 'I'm just taking back what's mine.' The two ברייתות no longer clash, and that supports רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this: the גמרא's way of drawing a proof

steps.whatToRemember: When a man has already arranged the match (שדיך), a woman's silence when receiving קידושין counts as agreement. Without that, her silence proves nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
this one is where he had arranged the match,
phrases.notes: This is the grabbing case, where she is מקודשת.

phrases.english: that one is where he had not arranged it.
phrases.notes: This is the debt-repayment case from step 11, where she is not מקודשת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash raised in step 15 by applying רב נחמן's distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's distinction is proven: silence counts as consent only when the match was arranged beforehand.

steps.title: The חכמים gather to collect רבי אסי's teachings
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. After רבי אסי died, the חכמים came together to gather and review his teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אסי passed away, the חכמים came in to gather up his teachings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a short story. This is a setup line that leads into the teachings quoted in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. The story explains why a series of רבי אסי's teachings is about to be quoted: the חכמים were collecting them after his death.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (literally: his soul rested)

phrases.english: When רבי אסי passed away,
the חכמים came in
to gather up his teachings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the proof about שדיך is finished.

steps.title: Land, like a woman, needs at least a פרוטה's worth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי אסי in the name of רבי מני: just as a woman cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth, land cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth either.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים, named רבי יעקב, said to them: This is what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני: Just as a woman cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth, so too land cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The first teaching of רבי אסי is quoted. It compares buying land to קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know קידושין with money needs at least a פרוטה's worth. This teaching says land works the same way: paying less than a פרוטה does not acquire it.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin that has legal value
Just as... so too: a comparison

phrases.english: One of the חכמים said to them,
and רבי יעקב was his name:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי:
phrases.english: This is what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני:
Just as a woman cannot be acquired
with less than a פרוטה's worth,
so too land cannot be acquired
with less than a פרוטה's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first teaching the חכמים collected, as set up in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Land, like a woman, cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth.

steps.title: A ברייתא says land CAN be acquired with less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יעקב from a ברייתא that says the opposite: a woman cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה, but land can.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Even though a woman cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth, land can be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack the teaching from step 18 using a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי's teaching treats land and a woman the same. The ברייתא openly separates them: a woman needs a פרוטה, land does not. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opening a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to him: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין אִשָּׁה נִקְנֵית
phrases.english: Even though a woman cannot be acquired
with less than a פרוטה's worth,
land can be acquired with less than a פרוטה's worth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 18 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's teaching that land cannot be acquired with less than a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says land can be acquired with less than a פרוטה, even though a woman cannot.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about acquiring through חליפין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב answers that the ברייתא is talking about חליפין, an exchange done by handing over an object, where the object does not need to be worth a פרוטה. רבי אסי was talking about buying land with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about חליפין, as it is taught: One can acquire with a utensil, even though it is not worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב defends רבי אסי's teaching by showing the ברייתא is about a different way of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חליפין, the buyer hands over an object as a sign of the deal, so its value doesn't matter. That is why land can be acquired 'with less than a פרוטה' in the ברייתא. רבי אסי meant buying land with money, which needs at least a פרוטה, just like קידושין with money.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring by exchange: handing over an object to finalize a deal

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא and רבי אסי don't disagree. They are talking about two different ways of acquiring land: money needs a פרוטה, חליפין does not.

phrases.english: He said to them:
When that ברייתא was taught, it was about חליפין,
as it is taught: One can acquire with a utensil,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: even though it is not worth a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by limiting the ברייתא to חליפין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a different method of acquisition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means land can be bought with money worth less than a פרוטה, which contradicts רבי אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about חליפין, where value doesn't matter. Buying land with money still needs a פרוטה.

steps.title: שמואל: Whoever doesn't know the laws of divorce and קידושין should stay away
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים continue with another teaching. They first quote שמואל's rule that anyone who doesn't know the laws of גיטין and קידושין should not get involved with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They then sat and said: That which רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Anyone who does not know the nature of divorces and קידושין should not have any dealings with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים go on to another of רבי אסי's teachings. First the גמרא quotes שמואל's rule, which sets up רבי אסי's addition in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל warns that only someone who truly knows these laws should handle a גט or קידושין. This rule is the base that רבי אסי builds on next.

keyTerms.meaning: They sat again, they went back to discussing
The nature or details of something

phrases.english: They then sat and said:
phrases.notes: They are still going through רבי אסי's teachings. This next one is his addition to שמואל's rule.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: That which רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
Anyone who does not know
the nature of divorces and קידושין
should not have any dealings with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another teaching collected from רבי אסי, beginning with the rule of שמואל that he builds on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who does not know the laws of גיטין and קידושין should not get involved with them.

steps.title: They are worse for the world than דור המבול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, adds that such unqualified people are worse for the world than דור המבול, and quotes a פסוק from הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And they are worse for the world than דור המבול, as it says: 'Swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and adultery; they break out, and blood touches blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי adds a strong warning to שמואל's rule: people who handle these laws without knowing them do terrible damage to the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said such people should stay away. רבי אסי adds how serious it is: mistakes with גיטין and קידושין are worse than the sins of דור המבול. The פסוק is quoted as the source, and steps 23-25 explain how it proves this.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the Flood in נח's time

steps.whatToRemember: Handling גיטין and קידושין without proper knowledge is not a small mistake. שמואל says to stay away, and רבי אסי says such people are worse for the world than דור המבול.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
And they are worse for the world
phrases.notes: 'They' means people who handle גיטין and קידושין without knowing the laws.

phrases.english: than the generation of the Flood,
as it says:
'Swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and adultery;
they break out, and blood touches blood.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְקָשִׁין לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי אסי's own warning on top of שמואל's rule from step 21, with a פסוק as its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who handle גיטין and קידושין without knowledge are worse for the world than דור המבול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the laws of גיטין and קידושין are handled only by experts: a mistake here has very serious results.

steps.title: How do we know the פסוק is about these people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק from הושע shows that unqualified people in גיטין and קידושין are worse than דור המבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where in the פסוק can we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we can see from the פסוק that רבי יוחנן's statement is true. This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, רבי יוחנן quoted a פסוק from הושע, but it is not obvious how that פסוק is about גיטין and קידושין, or how it shows these people are worse than דור המבול. The גמרא now asks for both of these points to be shown from the text.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? How is this learned from the text?

phrases.english: From where is it inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוחנן's פסוק proves his claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק in הושע refers to unqualified people in גיטין and קידושין, and how it shows they are worse than דור המבול.

steps.title: רב יוסף's translation shows the פסוק is about children born from other men's wives
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף translates the פסוק as describing people who have children with other men's wives and keep adding sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translated it: They have children from their friends' wives, and they add sins on top of sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first part of the question. Using רב יוסף's Aramaic translation, it shows that the פסוק is talking about children born from forbidden relationships.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone who does not know the laws makes a bad גט or bad קידושין, a woman may remarry while she is still really married to her first husband. Her children from the second man are then born from "another man's wife." רב יוסף's translation shows that the פסוק is describing exactly this kind of damage.

keyTerms.meaning: As he translated it into Aramaic
The wives of their friends, meaning other men's wives

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translated:
phrases.notes: He's translating the end of הושע 4:2, "פָּרָצוּ וְדָמִים בְּדָמִים נָגָעוּ".

phrases.english: They give birth to children from the wives of their fellows;
they add sins upon sins,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the question: the פסוק is about forbidden children.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation reads the פסוק as describing children born from other men's wives.

steps.title: Even the fish will die, which did not happen in the מבול
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק says even the fish of the sea will be taken away. In דור המבול only creatures on dry land died, so this punishment is worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "Therefore the land mourns, and everyone who lives in it is miserable, with the animals of the field and the birds of the sky, and even the fish of the sea will be taken away." But in דור המבול no decree was made against the fish in the sea, as it says: "Everything on dry land died", and not the fish in the sea. But here, even the fish in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second part: that these people are worse than דור המבול. It compares the punishment in הושע, which reaches even the fish, with the מבול, which did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק right after the sins in הושע describes a punishment that includes the fish. The תורה says only what was "on dry land" died in the מבול, so the fish survived. A punishment that goes even further than the מבול shows that these sins are treated as worse.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's claim is built from two pieces: רב יוסף's translation shows the פסוק is about forbidden children, and the fish dying shows the punishment is bigger than the מבול.

phrases.english: And it is written: "Therefore the land mourns
and everyone who dwells in it languishes,
with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky,
and also the fish of the sea will be taken away, etc."
Whereas in the generation of the flood,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵירָה עַל דָּגִים שֶׁבַּיָּם.
phrases.english: no decree was made against the fish in the sea,
as it says: "Of all that was on dry land, they died"
and not the fish in the sea.
But here, even the fish in the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by proving the 'worse than דור המבול' part.
steps.raayaObject: That unqualified people in גיטין and קידושין are worse than דור המבול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 4:3 (even the fish are taken) compared with בראשית 7:22 (only those on dry land died in the מבול).

steps.title: Maybe the punishment comes only if all the sins are done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the punishment in הושע might come only when people commit every sin listed in the פסוק, not adultery alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it only happens once they do all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe the terrible punishment only comes if all the sins in the פסוק are done together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע lists several sins together, and only then describes the punishment. So maybe adultery and forbidden children alone would not bring this punishment. If so, the proof that these people by themselves are worse than דור המבול falls apart.

phrases.english: But say: not until he does all of them!
phrases.notes: "All of them" means every sin in that פסוק: false swearing, lying, murder, stealing, and adultery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from הושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that adultery alone brings a punishment worse than the מבול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The punishment follows a list of several sins, so it may require all of them together.

steps.title: False swearing alone makes the land mourn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge with a פסוק in ירמיהו showing that false swearing alone makes the land mourn. So each sin on its own is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because it is written: "For because of swearing the land mourns."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each sin is enough by itself. It brings a פסוק showing that one sin, false swearing, is enough to make the land mourn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו uses the same words, "the land mourns," for false swearing alone. That shows the punishment does not need the whole list of sins. By the same logic, adultery alone would also be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't think that; it can't enter your mind
An oath, here meaning a false oath

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "For because of swearing the land mourns."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּכְתִיב כִּי מִפְּנֵי אָלָה אָבְלָה הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a second פסוק showing that a single sin is enough for the punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The punishment requires all the listed sins together.
steps.terutzMaskana: One sin alone (shown with false swearing) brings the land's mourning.

steps.title: Maybe false swearing is different from the other sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe false swearing is especially severe and brings the punishment alone, while the other sins still need to come together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: swearing is a case by itself, and these other sins are a case by themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. Maybe false swearing is special, so the proof from ירמיהו does not apply to the other sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו only proves something about false swearing. If false swearing is more severe, it could bring the punishment alone while adultery still could not. This brings back the question from step 26 about whether adultery alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Separately; in a category of its own

phrases.english: But say: an oath is separate,
and these are separate!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ירמיהו's פסוק about false swearing to prove that each sin alone is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: False swearing may be uniquely severe, so what is true of it may not be true of the other sins.
